name: Hip 90/90 Rotation
description: The hip 90/90 rotation is an active mobility drill that trains the ability to transition the hips between internal and external rotation by moving both legs simultaneously from one 90-90 configuration to the opposite. Unlike the passive 90-90 stretch, this version is performed as a controlled active movement. It develops proprioceptive awareness of hip rotation and is used in hip rehabilitation, athletic movement prep, and general hip mobility programs.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the floor with both legs in a 90-90 configuration — front leg with the shin facing forward (external rotation), rear leg to the side with the shin facing back (internal rotation).
execution.setup_instructions: Use a mat. Hands can be placed on the floor beside the hips for support in early stages.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a 90-90 seated position.
Step 2: Internally rotate both hips simultaneously — the front knee drops inward and the rear knee drops toward the floor in front.
Step 3: Both legs pass through a brief neutral position in the middle.
Step 4: Continue rotating to arrive in the 90-90 position on the opposite side.
Step 5: Pause, then rotate back to the starting side. Each full trip counts as one rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe freely and steadily. Do not hold the breath.
common_mistakes: Using the hands heavily for support, which reduces core and hip engagement
Moving too quickly — this requires deliberate slow control at each stage
One hip excessively lagging behind the other
safety_considerations: If sharp hip or knee pain occurs, stop and consult a clinician
Avoid if currently experiencing acute hip labral symptoms without clinical clearance
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full transition from one 90-90 configuration to the other, with both hips as close to the floor as available range allows.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3–4 seconds per transition, 5–10 reps each direction × 2–3 sets.
coaching_cues: Rotate both hips at the same time, not one then the other
Move as far through each transition as your hip allows
Gradually reduce your hand support as you gain confidence
